pending_items.title: Israeli real estate company holds ‘Black Friday’ land sale in Brooklyn
pending_items.content:
An Israeli real estate group held a "Black Friday" event in Brooklyn on Wednesday, advertising property sales and promoting what activist group Pal-Awda termed "illegal settlement on stolen Palestinian land”.

Firecrackers, smoke bombs and eggs were thrown at protesters by pro-Israel demonstrators outside the real estate event.

Israel's CapitIL real estate agency held the event, selling property in Essen NY Deli in Brooklyn. CapitIL’s website advertises several properties in and around Jerusalem. None publicly advertised is in the occupied West Bank. Middle East Eye was not able to verify which part of Jerusalem the land being promoted was located in. East Jerusalem is occupied according to international law.

Pal-Awda, an organisation that advocates for Palestinian refugees' right of return to their homeland, organised the protest outside the real estate event.

A spokesperson for Pal-Awda called the event "discriminatory" and said they would protest the land sales “no matter where in Palestine the stolen land is located” and that “all of it was taken from dispossessed Palestinians, as part of the ongoing Zionist ethnic cleansing”.

A spokesperson for the group said that these land sales are only open to vetted Jewish Americans who often have no previous or familial ties to Israel, arguing that CapitIL has ties to land sales happening in the occupied West Bank.

“Whether advertised or not, CapitIL and the event's other Israeli real estate cohosts like First Israel Mortgage have consistently offered or financed properties in the occupied West Bank and East Jerusalem during these events.”

The group says that these land sales violate several state and federal laws, including “New York Property Law, New York Human Rights Law, and state and federal real estate and housing laws”.

On Avenue J, 200 pro-Palestine protesters were kenneled in with lines of New York Police Department (NYPD) officers on either end and pro-Israel protesters sandwiching them in on both sides. NYPD drones loomed overhead, monitoring activity in the area. Newsweek reported that around 200 pro-Israel demonstrators were present, citing the NYPD.

Protesters chanted: “Palestine is our demand. No peace on stolen land.”

Pro-Israeli agitators threw at least three firecrackers and a red smoke bomb into the crowd of pro-Palestine protesters.

NYPD told MEE that three people had been arrested, processed and released, but did not specify which group they were from.

“We are being confronted by a racist mob of bigots who believe that Palestine does not belong to Palestinians, but belongs to settlers from all over the world. The people of Gaza are being bombed and murdered for the crime of being Palestinian in the land of Palestine, while these greedy companies are selling their Palestinian land to prosperous Americans who have no connection to Palestine whatsoever,” Pal-Awda activist Bill D told MEE.

MEE has reached out to CapitIL and NYPD for further comment but did not receive a response by the time of publication.

Athena, a protester, was holding a sign depicting New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani pointing a gun with the words “Chief Executive of the SRG”, referring to the police department's Strategic Response Group.

Athena isn’t happy with Mamdani’s handling of Israel real estate land sale events in the city.

“We have a mayor who says that he's pro-Palestine and that he stands against the genocide. Yet he sends his police officers to defend Zionists selling stolen land in the United States,” she said.

Pal-Awda has four demands for the mayor. They are asking that he advance calls to the NY Attorney General Leticia James to investigate and audit "illegal Palestinian land sales" in the city; remove tax-exempt status from religious and educational institutions that host occupied West Bank land sale events; fire NY Police Commissioner Jessica Tish. They also want the mayor to “fully disband the Strategic Response Group (SRG) and its replacements that allow for the NYPD's ongoing brutalisation of our community”.

Mamdani announced the disbandment of the controversial SRG earlier this month, but officers in riot gear at the protest kenneling the demonstrators still wore shirts that said "Strategic Response Group".

The armour-clad SRG is made up of 500 highly trained NYPD officers who have become infamous for their “crowd control tactics” and mass arrests during protests in the city, where they use batons, tear gas, pepper spray and other “de-escalation” weapons on disruptive protesters.

The group came under particular scrutiny due to their crackdown on pro-Palestine protests at the height of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, particularly campus protests led by the student movement that started at Columbia University.

"The irony of the timing of Mamdani's announcement regarding the disbandment of the SRG is not lost on us tonight," a Pal-Awda representative said in a statement.

"We have no faith in the mayor's lofty words, when it is his NYPD that is trampling, strangling and brutalising those calling for the end of Zionist land theft in our city.

"Time and again, it becomes clear that all levels of city and state government - from Attorney General Letitia James, who allows illegal land sales to go unchecked, to Mayor Mamdani, who oversees the brutalisation of New Yorkers - remain deeply complicit in the sale of stolen Palestinian land."
